newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm, corporations sell dlrs.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm, corporations sell dlrs.

text.p: The Mexican peso gained ground to close stronger across the board after a quiet session on Thursday due to corporations selling dollars, traders said.

"As the month is just beginning, corporations tend not to have much cash and step in to sell dollars for pesos," a trader said. The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 0.35 and 1.1 centavos firmer, respectively, at 7.8215/7.8235 and 7.8100/7.8130 per dollar.
"We've had three very calm sessions with trading ranges so narrow there's little to do in the market," he added.

Traders said volume was thin and dealing light as the market was cautious ahead of U.S. non-farm payroll data to be released on Friday, which could have repercussions on U.S. interest rates, and hence on the peso.
"As the Federal Open Market Committee did not move rates (on Wednesday), the market sees data within expectations, but even so dealers prefer to wait and see," another trader said.
Same-day peso contracts closed earlier 0.75 of a centavo firmer at 7.8150/7.8175 per dollar.
